editorial.headline: Bonded Warehousing: Open Nationally, Registrable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Bonded warehousing operates physical commodity storage in bonded areas, with foreign ownership open nationally and a Bali route that survives the province’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Bonded warehouse activity is a narrowly defined storage operation inside the customs territory that receives special treatment as though it were outside that territory. In practical terms, the activity is the operation of places that store physical commodities within a bonded area. The point is the warehouse function itself: holding tangible goods in a specially treated customs setting. That definition gives the code its centre of gravity, rooted in the status of the storage area and the physical commodities kept there.

Registration is open across the full listed business-scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. This matters because the activity is not confined in the record to one end of the enterprise spectrum. A micro operator and a large operator appear within the same availability frame, provided each is registering this bonded-warehouse activity. The scale list establishes who may register the activity at each listed scale, while the operating scope remains the storage of physical commodities in a bonded area.

Nationally, the PMA position is TERBUKA: foreign investment is open, and the maximum foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In Bali, the reading requires more precision. The record does not mark PMA registration as blocked; it describes the Bali status as open on the higher-risk track. The provincial moratorium is permanent and island-wide for PMA entries falling into Low and Medium-Low risk. Yet the record places the Besar scale at Menengah Tinggi and states that it survives that moratorium. On that stated basis, a PT PMA may register this activity in Bali.

The result is neither a blanket Bali prohibition nor an assumption that national openness alone answers the provincial question. The national position is fully open to foreign ownership; the Bali outcome is likewise registrable because the activity’s recorded risk position is not within the moratorium’s blocked bands. The activity remains what its scope says it is—operation of physical-commodity storage in a bonded area—so both the ownership position and the Bali conclusion should stay tied to that exact activity.
